offlineAnswers.answer: Yes. At PwC, Sainik designed event-driven .NET 8 middleware using nine HTTP, Timer, and Azure Service Bus-triggered Functions across three decoupled queues. It used at-least-once delivery and five-stage exponential retry to automate SAP Ariba, Icertis CLM, and SAP ECC workflows, reducing contract turnaround from about seven days to under two hours.

Sainik integrated PayU using SHA512 signing and SURL/FURL callbacks, then designed an idempotent order-to-payment state machine that eliminated duplicate-cart race conditions. Payment success increased from 91% to 97.5%, recovering approximately ₹10 lakh per month in previously failed transactions.

Sainik designed a referral and loyalty subsystem across ASP.NET Identity, EF Core, and a .NET 8 Azure Function, including secure codes, self-referral protection, and idempotent Dynamics 365 synchronization. It drove a 22% lift in net-new signups, ₹1.4 Cr+ in incremental first-quarter GMV, and an approximately 18% reduction in paid CAC.

Sainik optimized Azure Cognitive Search and Redis with versioned tenant-aware cache keys, barcode lookup, empty-result protection, and live inventory enrichment. That reduced p95 latency from roughly 850 ms to 310 ms, raised cache hit rate from 58% to 84%, and improved search-to-cart conversion by about 9%.

Sainik architected a React 18 and TypeScript distributor-operations console for driver planning, drag-and-drop order assignment, bulk picker tasks, packing, and reconciliation across 15 warehouses. It reduced a three-to-four-hour dispatch process to under five minutes, cut pick-pack errors by about 65%, and increased warehouse throughput by about 35%.

Sainik built a React Native barcode and QR scanner with Vision Camera frame processors, off-UI-thread decoding, support for more than ten symbologies, haptic feedback, and live inventory-aware lookup. It reduced product-discovery time from about 25 seconds to under four seconds and increased scan-to-cart conversion by roughly 12%.

Yes—C#/.NET and ASP.NET Core are Sainik's primary backend stack. His documented work covers 12-13 service commerce platforms, REST APIs, EF Core and Dapper data access, .NET 8 Azure Functions, event-driven processing, payment workflows, and SAP/Salesforce integrations using layered architecture, dependency injection, and idempotency.

Sainik has production experience with .NET 8 isolated-worker Azure Functions. He used HTTP, Timer, and Service Bus triggers for referral synchronization, enterprise contract automation, and SAP/Salesforce data flows, with retry handling, idempotency, audit logging, and Application Insights observability.

Sainik's data work includes SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, EF Core, Dapper, indexing, query optimization, bulk processing, and Redis caching. In one D2C platform, query and repository optimization reduced average API latency from about 850 ms to 310 ms and lowered peak database CPU by roughly 35%.

Sainik has implemented Application Insights distributed tracing and centralized audit logging for Azure integrations, plus Prometheus/Grafana observability for Kubernetes services. His focus is actionable health, latency, processing-state, and failure visibility rather than log collection alone.

At Bespoke Labs-AI, Sainik packaged a FastAPI and PostgreSQL stack with Helm on Kubernetes, including Prometheus and Grafana. He also built a Docker-in-Docker k3d image that creates the cluster, imports application images, installs the charts, and exposes the environment through one reproducible bootstrap.

Sainik builds Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for .NET services, Azure Functions, containers, and Azure infrastructure. His documented delivery work includes Docker-to-ACR publishing, Azure deployments, zip deployment, ARM-templated provisioning, Helm releases, local Azurite testing, and release ownership for both mobile stores.

Sainik's strongest lane is backend software engineering with C#/.NET, ASP.NET Core, REST APIs, microservices, Azure Functions, SQL, EF Core, Dapper, Redis, and enterprise integrations. He also ships React/TypeScript and React Native products and supports them with Azure DevOps, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Application Insights, Prometheus, and Grafana.

Sainik is a Lead Software Engineer (Associate) at PwC India, where he works on B2B and D2C commerce platforms and pharmaceutical enterprise integrations. His scope covers .NET microservices, React/TypeScript operations tooling, Azure Functions and Service Bus, payments, search and caching, databases, CI/CD, and production observability.

As a DevOps Engineer Intern at Bespoke Labs-AI, Sainik deployed a FastAPI/PostgreSQL microservice stack through Helm on Kubernetes with Prometheus/Grafana observability. He then built a Docker-in-Docker k3d environment that could reproduce the complete stack from a single image.

During a remote Data Science Research Internship with UC Berkeley Haas, Sainik analysed more than 10 million population-census records, applied machine-learning methods to district population forecasting, and prepared statistical research reports.
Sainik earned a Bachelor of Engineering in Electrical Engineering from Jadavpur University in 2024 with a CGPA of 8.33/10. His listed Microsoft certifications are AZ-204 and AZ-400.

Sainik's documented impact includes platforms serving 3,500+ retailers at ₹8-10 Cr monthly GMV, ₹1.4 Cr+ incremental referral GMV, a 22% signup lift, payment success growth from 91% to 97.5%, and search latency reduced by 63%. These figures come from specific commerce and integration engagements rather than generic portfolio estimates.

Sainik is open to remote opportunities and willing to relocate. He is best aligned with backend or full-stack roles involving C#/.NET, APIs, distributed workflows, SQL, Azure, integrations, and production ownership. Share your stack and hardest engineering problem for a more specific fit assessment.
